record.context_brief: Best universal upper bound refining Hermite-Hadamard
record.original_question: Let f: I -> R be a convex C^infinity function on an interval I, and for a < b in I define N(alpha, beta) = alpha(f(a) + f(b)) + beta f((a + b)/2) with 2alpha + beta = 1. Determine the best possible constants alpha* and beta* for which the upper Hermite-Hadamard-type inequality (1/(b - a)) integral_a^b f(t) dt <= N(alpha*, beta*) holds for every such smooth convex function and every choice of a < b in I. Equivalently, find the smallest universal endpoint weight alpha* such that alpha*(f(a) + f(b)) + (1 - 2alpha*) f((a + b)/2) always dominates the integral mean of every smooth convex function. The paper shows that N(1/4, 1/2) works for all convex integrable functions, and that the sharper candidate N(1/6, 2/3) is best possible only under the additional assumption that f'' is convex (equivalently, f^(4) >= 0), so the universal optimum for all smooth convex functions remains open.

evidence.quote: We found the value N(1/4, 1/2) for which the right-hand side of (1.3) holds for any integrable convex function.

Therefore we obtain a potentially best possible bound N(1/6, 2/3). Unfortunately, as is shown in Theorem 2.6, this bound is best possible only for the class of differentiable convex functions for which f^(4)(t) >= 0, t in I.
Open Question Find the best possible bound N(alpha*, beta*) valid for all convex mappings from the class C^infinity(I).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real interval $I$, let $f \in C^\infty(I)$ be convex, and for $a < b$ in $I$ and real numbers $\alpha,\beta$ with $2\alpha+\beta=1$ define
$$N(\alpha,\beta;f,a,b) := \alpha\bigl(f(a)+f(b)\bigr) + \beta\, f\!\left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right).$$
The classical Hermite–Hadamard inequality states that for every convex $f$ and every $a<b$ in $I$,
$$f\!\left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right) \le \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(t)\,dt \le \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(f(a)+f(b)\bigr),$$
i.e., the upper bound corresponds to $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/2,0)$ and the lower bound to $(0,1)$.

It is known that the choice $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/4,1/2)$ yields a valid upper bound
$$\frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(t)\,dt \;\le\; \tfrac{1}{4}\bigl(f(a)+f(b)\bigr)+\tfrac{1}{2}f\!\left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right)$$
for every integrable convex $f$, and that the sharper choice $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/6,2/3)$ provides a valid (and best possible) upper bound under the additional hypothesis that $f''$ is convex on $I$ (equivalently, $f^{(4)}\ge 0$ when $f\in C^4$).

Determine the best possible pair $(\alpha^*,\beta^*)$ with $2\alpha^*+\beta^*=1$ such that
$$\frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(t)\,dt \;\le\; \alpha^*\bigl(f(a)+f(b)\bigr) + \beta^*\, f\!\left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right)$$
holds for every $C^\infty$ convex function $f$ on $I$ and every $a<b$ in $I$. Equivalently, find the smallest universal endpoint weight $\alpha^*$ such that
$$\alpha^*\bigl(f(a)+f(b)\bigr) + (1-2\alpha^*) f\!\left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right) \;\ge\; \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(t)\,dt$$
for all such $f$ and all $a<b$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for refinements of the Hermite–Hadamard upper bound with weights $(1/4,1/2)$ and $(1/6,2/3)$ surfaces general literature on Hermite–Hadamard-type inequalities and tight versions, but no source could be located that resolves the universal optimum over all $C^\infty$ convex functions. The status of the problem appears unverified from public sources.

status_evidence.title: A tight Hermite–Hadamard inequality and a generic method for comparison between residuals
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tight Hermite–Hadamard inequalities and comparison of residuals for convex functions, but does not address the specific universal $(\alpha^*,\beta^*)$ optimum.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on tight Hermite-Hadamard bounds exists but does not resolve this specific universal optimum.

status_evidence.title: Improved Bounds for Hermite-Hadamard Inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Studies improved bounds in Hermite–Hadamard inequalities under regularity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Improved/refined bounds are studied but the universal best constant for smooth convex functions is not pinned down here.
